purpose: Free, structured retention education that compounds trust and routes qualified people towards deeper help without turning every lesson into a sales post.

categories.name: Retention Foundations
categories.promise: Understand why customers return, lapse and disappear, and what a healthy retention system needs before tactics.

categories.name: Lifecycle Systems
categories.promise: Design the journeys, triggers, timing and exclusions that make follow-up useful rather than noisy.

categories.name: Revenue Recovery
categories.promise: Find missed enquiries, weak follow-up, overdue customers and other recoverable demand before buying more traffic.

categories.name: CRM & Automation
categories.promise: Turn customer data into reliable workflows with fewer manual hand-offs and clearer ownership.

categories.name: Deliverability
categories.promise: Build sending practices that protect inbox placement, consent, reputation and long-term reach.

categories.name: Measurement & Testing
categories.promise: Measure the customer and commercial outcome, not just opens, clicks and activity.

categories.name: Breakdowns
categories.promise: Learn from real, permission-safe examples, teardowns and annotated systems without fake proof.

seasonModel.definition: A bounded learning sequence inside one category with a single learner outcome.
requirements: no filler lesson created merely to hit a count

initialSeasons.title: Season 1: The Client Return System
initialSeasons.outcome: Map the moments between first enquiry and repeat business and identify where customers currently fall out.
lessons: Why a booking reminder is not a retention system
The five return moments every appointment-led business should map
What happens after the first visit
The exclusions that stop useful follow-up becoming spam

initialSeasons.title: Season 2: Recover Before You Acquire
initialSeasons.outcome: Audit the revenue already sitting inside enquiries, follow-up gaps and dormant customer relationships before spending more on acquisition.
lessons: The four places demand usually disappears
How to decide whether the opportunity is commercially worth fixing

paidLayer.rule: Do not publish pricing, availability, entitlements or guarantees until the specific paid offer is separately verified and approved.

publishingRules: Every Retention School post must map to a category and either a season, resource or standalone diagnostic lesson.
Do not repost 222Emails promotional copy merely to keep the channel active.
Free lessons should be useful without requiring a sales call.
Use a commercial CTA only when it is the natural next step for the lesson.
Preserve proof safety and permission boundaries.
